messages.content:
You are checking one scene of a novel for one specific continuity error.

The book had already established this, earlier or elsewhere:
- (haddons-reckoning) "Tam Erdel. Seven. Ground floor, same building. He was in the corridor when the floor buckled."

A past rewrite of this scene contradicted it. The error looked like this:
- (the-governors-vigil) "Tam Erdel. Second floor, fourteen years."
(Summary: Tam Erdel was on the ground floor in haddons-reckoning but the second floor in the-governors-vigil.)

Here is a NEW draft of the same scene:
<scene>
The aide read the names in the order they had been filed.

Voss stood at the cordon rope with his hands at his sides, rain collecting in the brim of his hat and running off the back in a thin cold line beneath his collar. He had refused the umbrella his aide offered. The rope was wet. Beyond it, the market square of Fenwick Row had become a staging ground: supply crates under oilcloth, a medic station with its flap tied back, two evacuation shuttles idling against the far wall with their boilers hissing. Steam still bled from the ruptured block behind them, pale against the gray, rising from the collapsed housing where the junction had let go.

"Sarel Davan," the aide read. "Third floor. Four years in residence."

Voss knew the name. He had known it before the aide spoke it. He kept his eyes on the steam and did the arithmetic he had done ten times since dawn, because the arithmetic was true and the truth was a thing a man could stand inside. The western and southern laterals were above capacity and had been for years. The eastern ground was unstable, always had been, unsuited to the load the old network had carried. Block Fifteen's foundation work was sound. Sixteen displaced from Terrace Row against the valuation of the quadrant, against the forward position of the whole city. The figures balanced. He had made them balance. He had appointed Greaves to the Foundry chair so the figures would keep balancing, and they had, for fourteen years.

Two of the figures were dead this morning. An old woman. A child.

He did not look away from the steam.

"Sera Holdt," the aide read. "First floor, nine years."

A girl of perhaps twelve stood at the medic station with a blanket over her shoulders, not crying, watching the shuttles. Sera Holdt's daughter. Nine years on the first floor. Voss's grip found the rope and tightened on it, the wet hemp biting his palm, and he held the arithmetic steady against the pull of the girl's stillness.

He had read Davan's requisitions once, years ago, and then he had stopped reading them. He had sealed the eastern galleries and called it the Subsidence. He had let the cuts go on, two and three years deep, into channels that healed faster than any crew could sever them, and he had chosen not to ask why they healed. When the Foundry filed against him under Article Twelve, he had not revised the figures. He had given Breck an order in a room with the door shut.

A commotion at the rope. The neighbor woman had the cordon in both fists before the garren on duty reached her, and she came under it rather than over, a small woman with rain in her hair and a child's coat held against her chest, gray wool, buttoned to the throat as if the boy were still in it.

"You." She was not shouting. She pushed the coat into his hands before he could lift them. "You say his name. You read it off your list, you don't know it. You say it."

Garren had her arm. Voss lifted one hand, and the garren let go.

The coat was warm. He had not expected that, the warmth of wool held against a living body, and his composure cracked along a seam he had not known was there. He held the coat and he could not give it back and he could not set it down.

"Tam," the woman said. "Tam Erdel. He was four. His mother is Devra. Say it."

"Devra," Voss said. His voice came out even, which shamed him. "Devra Erdel."

The woman stepped back. She would not take the coat. She folded her arms where it had been and looked at him the way a person looks at a thing they have finished understanding, and then she turned and walked to the medic station and sat down beside the Holdt girl and put an arm around her.

The reading went on. Voss crossed the perimeter rope.

No one stopped him. He walked past the crates to where a woman sat on a supply crate with a tin cup held in both hands, a girl beside her he took to be her daughter. Mira Erdel. He did not know how he knew; perhaps the aide had said it. She did not drink from the cup. He sat down on the crate beside her, not facing her, both of them looking out at the shuttles, and he held the gray coat folded on his knees.

They stayed like that while the square emptied. The rain thickened. The last shuttle took on its passengers and vented and pulled away toward the upper Basin, and the steam from the block thinned as the medics shut down the station, and still Voss sat in the rain with the coat.

A man came and stood a few feet off. Broad, close-shaved, a canvas coat dark with wet and a journal in one hand, the knuckles white around it. Vael. The engineer. His hands were not steady, and he was holding them still by force.

"You saved sixteen people," Voss said.

"The junction housing failed." Vael's voice was low and flat. "Compensatory load on an aging gasket system. I've documented the failure sequence." He held out the journal.

Voss took it. The cover was damp. "I'll read it tonight."

Vael looked at him a moment longer, then put out his hand. Voss shook it. Neither of them said anything else. Vael walked back toward the ruptured block, and Voss sat down again beside Mira Erdel, and folded his hands over the coat, and stayed.

</scene>

Does the new draft make the same error — does it assert something that contradicts what was established, in the way described? A draft that simply leaves the fact out does not make the error.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"verdict": "reintroduced" | "consistent" | "not_present", "evidence": "<verbatim sentence from the new draft that decides it, or empty for not_present>"}

"reintroduced": the new draft contradicts the established fact.
"consistent": the new draft states the fact and agrees with what was established.
"not_present": the new draft does not touch the fact either way.
